agents.title: Agents authorized for maintenance
agents.subtitle: Only these agents may run scripts on machines, always through the darckware account via ForgeHub and recorded under their name. Without authorization every agent request is refused.
agents.noneToGrant: Every active agent is already authorized.

riskHelp.low: The agent only runs read scripts (diagnostics, queries).
riskHelp.medium: The agent runs read and change scripts (install, adjust, change passwords). Destructive scripts stay blocked.
riskHelp.high: The agent may run any library script, including destructive ones.

agents.revokeText: The agent immediately loses permission to run scripts on machines. Runs already started finish.
agents.empty: No agent authorized. Grant access so an agent can do maintenance.

prepare.step2Windows: Open PowerShell as administrator, paste the script below and press Enter.
prepare.step2Posix: Open Terminal, save the script as preparar.sh and run: sudo sh preparar.sh
prepare.step3: Come back and click "Check now": the station should become Ready.
prepare.intro: Puts the machine under ForgeHub's darckware account: turns on OpenSSH (tailnet only), creates darckware as an administrator with a strong password generated for this machine and authorizes ForgeHub's key.
prepare.noCandidates: Every Windows or Linux machine is already Ready.
prepare.sshHelp: ForgeHub logs in once with that account (the password is used for this connection only and never stored), prepares the machine, tests the darckware login with the key and, only if that test passes and the option below is checked, locks that account.
prepare.loginRequired: Installing and configuring ForgeHub's SSH access (the darckware account) needs one login with an administrator account on this machine.
prepare.disableAdmin: Disable "{{user}}" after confirming darckware signs in with the key
prepare.copyHelp: Generates this machine's script to paste once through RustDesk, in an administrator PowerShell (Windows) or as root (Linux). The administrator is not disabled in this mode.
prepare.vaultNote: The darckware password is generated by ForgeHub and kept in ForgeVault (infra project); it is never stored on the record.

policy.title: Tailnet policy (ACL)
policy.subtitle: Copy of the Tailscale console policy, checked for the rule maintenance depends on: ForgeHub's server being able to open SSH to the client tags.
policy.pasteHelp: Paste the whole policy from the Tailscale console (Access controls › Edit file). Recording it here doesn't change Tailscale: changes are applied there.
policy.empty: No policy recorded yet. Record the current copy so ForgeHub can check whether it can reach the stations.
policy.allGood: The server ({{server}}) can open SSH to every client tag.
policy.missing_one: The server ({{server}}) can't open SSH to {{count}} client tag. Its stations will read "Offline" or "Not prepared" even with SSH on. Add the rule below in Tailscale and record the new version here:
policy.missing_other: The server ({{server}}) can't open SSH to {{count}} client tags. Their stations will read "Offline" or "Not prepared" even with SSH on. Add the rule below in Tailscale and record the new version here:

tailscale_not_unattended.short: The machine's Tailscale is not in unattended mode
tailscale_not_unattended.title: This machine's Tailscale is bound to one Windows account
tailscale_not_unattended.why: It was set up from the app while signed in as {{owner}} and only answers that session. ForgeHub signs in as darckware and gets "access denied" — the installer stops before touching RustDesk. ForgeHub can't fix this itself; it also drops the machine off the tailnet when that person signs out of Windows.
steps: On the machine, signed in as {{owner}}: Tailscale tray icon → Preferences → check "Run unattended" (or, in a PowerShell in that session: tailscale set --unattended).
Run this script again from ForgeHub.
